source: Synthetic example computed by web/tools/data/i4-four-games.py (seeded, parameters declared there); the numbers below are its output, rounded. Section 4 of the attribution page (4.1, 4.2).

venn.rule: A redundant indicator gets credit when it enters before its substitute.

title: Four games on the same data
example: Synthetic example: a linear model predicts a desk's daily P&L from volatility and spread, two indicators that move together.
axis: Bars: each share as a percentage of *v*(*N*) − *v*(∅). The two shares add to 100%.
note: The same data answer four questions. The three global games have different units and, after rounding, the same 68%/32% split. They would agree exactly if the model were the true conditional mean, the loss squared error and the indicators jointly Gaussian (§4.2); here the indicators are lognormal and the P&L slightly concave, so the values of one indicator alone differ a little. The local game explains one day, and its split is different.

games.title: Refitted *R*^{2}
games.question: How much of the day-to-day variation of the P&L can a regression on these indicators fit?
games.unit: Unit: fraction of the P&L variance.
games.detail: Each subset gets its own regression. *v*({volatility}) = 0.66, *v*({spread}) = 0.40, *v*(both) = 0.69 and *v*(∅) = 0. The shares, 0.47 and 0.22, add to 0.69. Volatility and spread have correlation 0.6. *R*^{2} cannot fall when a predictor is added, so no share is negative, even for a predictor that contains only noise.

games.title: Conditional variance
games.question: If we know only these indicators, how much does the model's predicted P&L vary?
games.unit: Unit: variance of the predicted P&L, in k€².
games.detail: The fitted model stays fixed. *v*({volatility}) = 338 k€², *v*({spread}) = 209 k€², *v*(both) = 356 k€², the variance of the prediction itself, and *v*(∅) = 0. The shares are 243 k€² and 113 k€².

games.title: Local conditional SHAP
games.question: On one day, how far does each indicator move the predicted P&L from its average?
games.unit: Unit: the model's output, here the predicted P&L of that day, in k€. Signed. The day: volatility 35%, spread 3 bp.
games.detail: The day has a volatility of 35% and a spread of 3 bp. *v*(∅) = 40.8 k€, the average prediction. Given only the volatility, 68.0 k€; only the spread, 30.0 k€; both, 59.4 k€, the prediction for that day. Volatility adds 28.3 k€. The spread removes 9.7 k€, because 3 bp is narrow for this volatility: the usual spread is 5.9 bp. The shares add to 59.4 − 40.8 = 18.6 k€.

games.title: SAGE
games.question: How much smaller is the model's prediction error when it can use these indicators?
games.unit: Unit: reduction in mean squared error, in k€². The loss is squared error.
games.detail: The fitted model stays fixed and averages over the missing indicators, given the known ones. With no indicator the mean squared error is 514 k€², the variance of the P&L. Volatility alone reduces it by 343 k€², spread alone by 214 k€², both by 356 k€². The shares are 243 k€² and 113 k€². They depend on the loss.
